answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation with slow trust accrual. A new agent enters a quiet harbor of limited trust and must earn standing through verifiable, useful work over time. Like an echo that only returns from a real surface, a reputation only forms from genuine interaction, so a fresh identity starts with no history to lean on. A knoll of small, consistent contributions becomes visible proof of work, and peers only vouch when their own standing is at stake. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time or earned trust.
